# shopfront

A tiny order service used as the fixture for Junior-dev's headless runs. Customers place
orders through `POST /orders`; the service checks stock, charges the card through the
payment provider, and records the order. Orders are kept in `data/orders.json`.

# Checkout flow: placing an order

Sequence of `place_order()` in `src/app.py`. Stock and prices are in-memory dicts; orders are appended to `data/orders.json`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Caller
    participant A as app.place_order
    participant S as STOCK
    participant P as payments.charge
    participant F as data/orders.json

    C->>A: place_order(customer, items, card_token)

    loop each item in items
        A->>S: STOCK.get(name, 0)
        S-->>A: units in stock
    end
    Note over A,S: Unknown items read as 0 stock, so they are rejected

    alt any item has less stock than requested
        A-->>C: rejected, out of stock
    else enough stock for every item
        A->>P: charge(card_token, total(items))
        Note over P: Stub: no token means ok=false, otherwise always ok
        alt payment not ok
            P-->>A: {ok: false}
            A-->>C: rejected, payment failed
        else payment ok
            P-->>A: {ok: true, id: pay_...}
            Note over A,S: Stock is decremented only after payment succeeds
            A->>S: STOCK[name] -= qty
            A->>F: read orders, append order, write file
            Note over A,F: Order id = number of existing orders + 1
            A-->>C: placed, with order
        end
    end
```

## Notes

- **Stock check and decrement are not atomic.** Two concurrent calls can both pass the check and oversell.
- **No rollback.** If the file write fails after a charge, the card is charged, stock is decremented, and no order is saved.
- **`amount_cents` is ignored.** `charge()` never uses the amount it receives.
- **No input validation.** Quantities and item names are not checked beyond the stock lookup.
- **Stock resets on restart.** `STOCK` lives in memory; only orders persist.
- **README gaps.** The README mentions `POST /orders` and an email receipt. Neither exists in the code: `app.py` has no HTTP route and no email logic.
